card.statement:
Consider the space $M=(\mathbb C \mathbb P^1)^n$ with diagonal action of $G=SL(2)$. By Example <<ref:exPoints>>, $M^{s}=M^{ss}$ if and only if $n$ is odd. Take the maximal
compact subgroup $SU(2)$ of $G$. Its dual Lie algebra can be
identified with the real vector space $\mathbb R^3$. The
corresponding moment map takes the $n$-tuple of points on unit
sphere to their sum in $\mathbb R^3$. Then the fiber $\mu^{-1}(0)$
consists of the points with the center of gravity in the origin.
It is not hard to check directly that $\mu^{-1}(0)\subset M^{ss}$.
In the case when $n=4$ it can be straightforwardly proved that
$(\mathbb C \mathbb P^1)^n//SL(2)$ and $\mu^{-1}(0)/SU(2)$ are isomorphic to
a sphere $\mathbb C \mathbb P^1$ without three removed points. We refer the reader to
<<cite:MumfordForganyKirwan>> for the details.
card.label: Example 24

paper.title: Representations of posets: Linear versus Unitary
paper.abstract: A number of recent papers treated the representation theory of partially ordered sets in unitary spaces with the so called orthoscalar relation. Such theory generalizes the classical theory which studies the representations of partially ordered sets in linear spaces. It happens that the results in the unitary case are well-correlated with those in the linear case. The purpose of this article is to shed light on this phenomena.
